summary: Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy and studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She earned her Dr. phil. and completed her Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her posts include positions at Freie Universität Berlin, the University of British Columbia, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

Karl Albert Agathon Benary was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He earned doctorates from Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg and studied under Franz Bopp. He served as a Gymnasiallehrer at Cöllnisches Gymnasium and Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Karl Ammer was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna, studying under Geiger, Frauwallner, Trubetzkoy, and Havers. He held posts as librarian, assistant, PD, and director at Vienna before directing Halle-Wittenberg's Indology Institute.

Karl Benedikt Hase worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Jena, Helmstedt, and under Silvestre de Sacy. His posts included roles at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, École Polytechnique, and the University of Paris.

Karl Bernhard Seidenstücker worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch after studies at Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg. He worked as an assistant at Museum am Rothenbaum and founded several German Buddhist organizations.

Karl Bohnenberger was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Eduard Sievers. He spent his career at Tübingen as a librarian, Privatdozent, extraordinary professor, and ordinary professor of German.

Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig (Ph.D., Habilitation), and Bonn under Curtius, Ritschl, and Zarncke. He taught at Alte Nikolaischule, the University of Freiburg, and the University of Leipzig.

Karl Brunnhölzl works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.
Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle. He served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Karl Dyroff was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology who attended the Kronberg Gymnasium Aschaffenburg. He held an academic post at the University of Munich from around 1898 to 1938.

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. After attending Sächsisches Landesgymnasium Sankt Afra, he studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, later serving on the faculty at Heidelberg University from around 1842 to 1845.

Karl Eugen Neumann worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Leipzig, completing his Ph.D. under Richard Pischel and Ernst Windisch.
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. From around 1856 to 1882, he held posts at both the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Olof August Danielsson and Per Persson. He spent his academic career at Uppsala University, serving successively as Privatdozent, acting professor, extraordinary professor, and professor.

Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and studying at Berlin. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and the University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Burkhard was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Halle-Wittenberg (PhD), and Munich. He served as a Gymnasial Professor in Teschen and Vienna, and later as director of the Franz-Joseph-Gymnasium Wien.

Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist and Iranologist who studied at Leipzig and Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth). He held academic posts at the universities of Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, and Marburg.

Karl Friedrich Hermann was a scholar of history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg and Leipzig under Friedrich Creuzer and Gottfried Hermann, and held posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Marburg, and the University of Göttingen.

Karl Friedrich Keil worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at the University of Tartu and Humboldt University of Berlin, later serving at Tartu as Privatdozent and Professor of Exegetics and Oriental Languages.
